reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of runs expectancy lies in decomposing inning dynamics into discrete states defined by outs and runner configurations. Each state maps to a probability distribution over runs scored, forming a stochastic kernel. The multinomial framework extends this to model inter-team variability, assuming each team's run-scoring follows a distinct distribution parameterized by latent variables. Ordinal regression then introduces structured dependencies among these parameters, allowing inference on how external factors like park or pitcher quality alter run-scoring behavior. The failure mode occurs when the independence or stationarity assumptions break down—such as during high-leverage clutch moments or when teams exhibit non-stationary performance. These primitives form a dual system: one for static expectation and another for dynamic adaptation.
